description: COSMIC84 builds innovative space-tech solutions. Our project, SafeSol, helps Mars crews find safe routes and shelters during solar storms using NASA data.
summary:
SafeSol is a web app that helps a crew on Mars plan a safe drive and find shelter during a solar storm. It is built on real NASA data for Jezero Crater: the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter CTX elevation model and orthoimage (processed by USGS Astrogeology), and solar storm events from NASA’s DONKI database.

For the challenge “Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map,” users draw a route on the map. SafeSol checks the slope every 25 m against the rover’s 20° limit, marks steep sections in red, and suggests a safe route. In a storm drill, users replay a real storm, such as September 10, 2017, with a chosen warning time. SafeSol then shows which shelters the crew can reach in time, or says that none can be reached.

This matters because on Mars a crew may have only minutes of warning. Every result comes from tested code (17 unit tests), not an AI model, so the numbers can be checked.
details:
What it does: SafeSol is a web app that plans rover drives and shelter during solar storms on Mars, using a real map of Jezero Crater. Users draw a route, and SafeSol samples the terrain slope every 25 m against the rover’s 20° limit. Steep segments turn red and the route fails with a clear reason. “Suggest safe route” finds a path under the limit using Dijkstra’s algorithm. In the storm drill, users pick a real solar storm (for example September 10, 2017) and a warning time. SafeSol shows a zone of shelters the crew can reach in time, or says that none can be reached.

Data: NASA MRO CTX elevation model and orthoimage of Jezero Crater (via USGS Astrogeology), and 24 solar energetic particle events from 2017 and 2024 from NASA’s DONKI database. A “Data sources and raw records” panel shows the raw records behind each result.

Benefits and impact: Crews and mission planners get a fast, checkable answer to two questions: is this route safe, and can we reach shelter before the storm arrives. Warning times on Mars can be minutes. The approach can later extend to live DONKI alerts, the Moon and Artemis.

Tools: Claude (Anthropic) was used throughout for system design, building the app (frontend and code), scripts, the video title card and the slide deck. The code and the live app are hosted on GitHub. No AI model runs inside the app. All results come from tested code (17 unit tests).

Creativity: SafeSol joins two NASA datasets, terrain and space weather, in one tool. It answers a decision a crew would actually face, and it reports honestly when no shelter is reachable.

Factors considered: Accuracy and traceability (real NASA data, raw records shown, tested code), realistic limits such as slope limit and warning time, and clear limitations: the shielding score is a relative index, not a radiation dose.
